AWARD/JUDGMENT 1.

The claim for compensation raised in the present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Satender Pal in a motor accident that took place on 06.12.2022 at about 7 PM, at NH-8, in front of Dhaula Kuan Metro Station towards Gurgaon,
Delhi, regarding which FIR No.424/22 was registered at PS Delhi Cantt.
2.

The offending vehicle involved in this case is an army truck bearing registration No. 14D193608M, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 Sh. Anuj Singh Yadav and owned by respondent no. 2 EETSU.
Case of the claimants 3.
It is the case of the claimants that the deceased was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No. HR-35E-8425 towards Gurgaon on NH-8.

When he reached Dhaula Kuan Metro Station at around 7 pm, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. 14D193608M, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a Misc DJ No. 175/23 Sushila Devi & Ors.

Vs. Anuj Singh Yadav & Anr. 02.04.2026 Page 2/29  rash and negligent manner and was running ahead of motorcycle of deceased, suddenly applied brakes in the middle of the road due to which motorcycle struck against the truck from behind.
It is further stated that the deceased was taken to RR Army Hospital where he succumbed to injuries during the course of his treatment.
Case of respondents no. 1 & 2 4.
Respondents no. 1 and 2 filed their reply to the DAR wherein it is stated that no such accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.
It is further stated that the police has falsely implicated them in the present matter.

It is further stated that as per CCTV footage, it is clearly evident that the vehicle in front of alleged offending Army vehicle applied brakes and in order to avoid collision, the respondent no. 1 also applied brakes.
It is further stated that the CCTV footage shows that the alleged offending vehicle was not over speeding and under the permissible speed limit.
It is stated that since the motorcycle had hit the truck from behind, the respondent was neither able to see it nor feel the impact of the accident due to heavy congestion and traffic at night.
It is further stated that the mechanical inspection report also reflects no damage to the Army Vehicle.
It is further stated that the accident took place due to negligence of deceased himself as he hit the motorcycle from behind.

sentences.text: I have heard arguments and have carefully perused the entire case record.
13. The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

ISSUE NO. 1 - Whether the deceased Sh. Satender Pal sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 06.12.2022 at about 7 PM, at NH-8, infront of Dhaula Kuan Metro Station towards Gurgaon, Delhi cause by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
14D193608M being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no.2? OPP.
14. Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimants.
The claimant no. 1 has examined herself as PW1.
Since PW1 is not an eye witness to the accident, her testimony cannot be considered for determining if the vehicle was being driven rashly and negligently.
15. The claimants examined Sh. Rambresh, an eye witness of the accident as PW3.

He deposed that he was on his rehdi near Dhaula Kuan Metro Station and saw at around 7 pm that an army truck bearing registration No. 14D193608M, which was being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly applied brakes in the middle of the road due to which the motorcyclist struck against the truck and motorcyclist fell down on the road.
He further deposed the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.

sentences.text: 16 . During cross-examination, he deposed that he was having his eyes on the road at the time of accident.
He further deposed that the offending vehicle was black colour army truck.
He stated that he noted the number of the truck on a piece of paper from a distance of 18-20 feet.

He disclosed that the number of the vehicle was 14D193608M.
17.

Ld. Counsel for respondents argued that the fact that PW3 even remembered the number of the truck establishes that he Sushila Devi vs Anuj Singh on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54230123/
4 was tutored by the claimants.
18. This Tribunal is of the view that merely because PW3 remembered the number of the truck does not establish that the entire testimony of the said witness is false.

Even though the witness was a vendor of eatables which he used to sell on a cart and therefore, may be uneducated, that by itself does not mean that he cannot remember the registration number of a vehicle.
19. The testimony of this witness is otherwise coherent and consistent.
It is also in consonance with the statement of Mr. Sayed Yasoob Hussain, which has been noted in the FIR.

20. Even though Mr. Sayed Yasoon Hussain did not step into the witness box, his statement can be considered by the Tribunal since it forms part of the DAR and contents of DAR are presumed to be correct in view of the decision in the case of Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & Ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021.

sentences.text: 21. The CCTV footage has been seen.
It is evident from the CCTV footage that the motorcyclist had struck against the truck.

In fact, this has also been admitted by the respondents themselves in their reply in which the following admissions have been made in paragraph no. 4 :-
i) "Since the motorcyclist had hit the army truck from behind."
ii) "The accident took place due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased, who hit the motorcycle from behind."
22.
The above admissions make it clear that the motorcyclist had indeed hit the army truck from behind.

Therefore,
the assertions of RW1 and RW2 as made by them in their respective evidence by way of affidavits Ex. RW1/A and Ex. PW2/A that the accident had not taken place with their vehicle is evidently false.

23. Merely because in the mechanical inspection report,
there is no damage to the truck that does not prove that the truck was not actually involved in the accident.
It is evident from the CCTV footage that the motorcyclist hit against the truck from behind.
24. In view of the evidence on record, it becomes necessary to ascertain as to why the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the truck had applied brakes.

If some other vehicle or person would have suddenly come in front of the truck, the truck would obviously Sushila Devi vs Anuj Singh on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54230123/
5
Misc DJ No. 175/23 Sushila Devi & Ors.
Vs. Anuj Singh Yadav & Anr. 02.04.2026 Page 8/29  have to be suddenly stopped.
As such, the reason for the respondent no.1 to have suddenly applied brakes is to be determined.
25. In this regard, the only testimony on record is that of RW1 and RW2 who are the driver and co-driver of the truck.
Thy both deposed that a vehicle in front suddenly applied brakes, due to which they had to also stop their vehicle.
26. It is evident from the CCTV footage that there was a car moving in front of the truck.
The car was moving at a much lower speed than the truck.
The respondent no. 1 was driving the truck at a higher speed and when it was about to hit the car, brakes were suddenly applied which suddenly stopped the truck.
It is pertinent to note that the car continued to move even after the accident of the motorcycle with the truck.
27. As such, the respondent no. 1 was rash and negligent by driving the truck at a speed higher than the speed of the car which was in front of the truck and by applying brakes to stop the truck.
When the respondent no. 1 was a distance where he could see the car in front moving at a slower speed, he should have also maintained a speed similar to that of the car.
Second circumstance which establishes the negligence of respondent no.1 is that he suddenly brought the truck to a halt even though the car in front continued to move.
28. There was no contributory negligence of the deceased.
It is evident from the CCTV footage that he was riding the motorcycle at a reasonable speed.
29. Due to the above rash and negligent driving of the Misc DJ No. 175/23 Sushila Devi & Ors. Vs. Anuj Singh Yadav & Anr.

Nothing material could be elicited from the cross-examination of PW3 to disbelieve or discard his testimony.
His testimony has been substantially corroborated with the DAR filed by the IO, the contents of which are presumed to be correct.

33.

In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on touchstone of preponderance of probability that Sh. Satender Pal sustained fatal injuries in the accident which took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. 14D193608M and the said vehicle at that time was being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimants and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2 - Whether the claimants are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
34.

As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No. 1 has been proved, the claimants have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the said accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
The compensation to which the claimants are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.

sentences.text: Page 15/29  "12.The law is well settled that deductions cannot be allowe  d from the amount of compensation either on  account of insurance, or on account of pensionary benefits  or gratuity or grant of employment to a kin of the deceased.
The main reason is that all these amounts are earned by the  deceased on account of contractual relations entered into by  him with others.
It cannot be said that these amounts  accrued to the dependents or the legal heirs of the deceased  on account of his death in a motor vehicle accident.

The  claimants/dependents are entitled to 'just compensation'
 under the Motor Vehicles Act as a result of the death of the  deceased in a motor vehicle accident.

Therefore, the natural  corollary is that the advantage which accrues to the estate  of the deceased or to his dependents as a result of some  contract or act which the deceased performed in his life time  cannot be said to be the outcome or result of the death of the  deceased even though these amounts may go into the hands  of the dependents only after his death."

52. In view of above Judgment and testimony of PW2 that the deceased would have got the amount at the time of retirement if he would have not died, it is held that the amounts received by the legal representatives are not liable to be deducted from the awarded amount of compensation.

(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 56.

To calculate compensation under the non-pecuniary heads, reference has to be drawn from decision in Pranay Sethi case (supra) wherein it was observed:
 ''...Unlike determination of income, the said heads  have to be quantified.
Any quantification must have a  reasonable foundation.
